muscles.name: Iliacus
muscles.actionText: Powerful hip flexor; assists external rotation of the femur and stabilises the pelvis.
muscles.clinical: Tightness can cause lower back and hip discomfort, and hip flexor strain from running and walking.

muscles.name: Psoas Major
origin: Transverse processes of T12 and all lumbar vertebrae (L1–L5)
muscles.actionText: Most powerful hip flexor; assists external rotation of the femur and pelvic stabilisation.
muscles.clinical: Tightness can cause lower back and hip discomfort, and hip flexor strain.

muscles.name: Rectus Femoris
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via the patellar tendon
muscles.actionText: The only quadriceps muscle crossing the hip joint: flexes the hip and extends the knee.
muscles.clinical: Weakness or tightness leads to limited hip extension or patellar tracking issues, common in runners and cyclists.

muscles.name: Sartorius
insertion: Proximal medial surface of the tibia at the pes anserinus
muscles.actionText: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation plus knee flexion — crossing the legs, kicking.
muscles.clinical: Tightness can cause anterior hip pain or inner thigh discomfort.
muscles.notes: Longest muscle in the body; the 'tailor's muscle'.

muscles.name: Gluteus Maximus
muscles.actionText: Hip extension (running, squatting), external rotation and abduction of the thigh.
muscles.clinical: Weakness leads to posterior pelvic tilt and low back pain — 'gluteal amnesia' in prolonged sitters.

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
insertion: Proximal medial surface of the tibia (pes anserinus)
muscles.actionText: Knee flexion, hip extension and internal rotation of the tibia when the knee is flexed.
muscles.clinical: Hamstring strains are among the most common athletic injuries; eccentric strengthening is central to rehab.

muscles.name: Semimembranosus
muscles.actionText: Knee flexion, hip extension and internal rotation of the tibia when the knee is flexed.
muscles.clinical: Works with semitendinosus to stabilise the knee and decelerate knee extension during running.

muscles.name: Biceps Femoris
origin: Short head: linea aspera of the femur
muscles.actionText: Knee flexion, hip extension and external rotation of the knee when flexed.
muscles.clinical: Long head is key in hip extension during sprinting; common site of hamstring tear.

muscles.name: Gluteus Medius
origin: Outer surface of the ilium (between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines)
muscles.actionText: Hip abduction and stabilisation of the pelvis during single-leg stance; the anterior fibres assist internal rotation of the thigh.
muscles.clinical: Weakness is associated with Trendelenburg gait — pelvis drops toward the non-weight-bearing leg.

muscles.name: Gluteus Minimus
origin: Outer surface of the ilium, just below the gluteus medius
muscles.actionText: Works with gluteus medius for hip abduction and internal rotation of the thigh.
muscles.clinical: Weakness leads to pelvic drop and hip instability.

muscles.name: Tensor Fasciae Latae
insertion: Iliotibial band (inserting into the lateral tibial condyle — Gerdy's tubercle)
muscles.actionText: Abducts, medially rotates and flexes the thigh; tenses the fascia lata to stabilise the knee in standing and walking.

muscles.name: Adductor Magnus
muscles.actionText: Hip adduction; the hamstring portion also contributes to hip extension.
muscles.clinical: Groin strains are common in athletes performing quick side-to-side movements.

muscles.name: Adductor Longus
muscles.actionText: Hip adduction; assists hip flexion.

muscles.name: Adductor Brevis
muscles.actionText: Hip adduction; assists hip flexion.

muscles.name: Pectineus
muscles.actionText: Adducts and flexes the thigh; assists medial rotation.

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.actionText: Adducts the thigh; flexes and medially rotates the leg at the knee.

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.actionText: External rotation and stabilisation of the hip joint.
muscles.clinical: Piriformis syndrome — the muscle irritates the sciatic nerve, causing posterior leg pain.

muscles.name: Gemelli (Superior & Inferior)
muscles.actionText: External rotation and stabilisation of the hip joint.

muscles.name: Obturator Internus
muscles.actionText: External rotation and stabilisation of the hip joint.

muscles.name: Obturator Externus
origin: Margin of bone immediately around the medial side of the obturator foramen
muscles.actionText: Lateral rotation of the hip.

muscles.name: Quadratus Femoris
muscles.actionText: External rotation and stabilisation of the hip joint.
muscles.notes: Spelled 'Quadrarus femoris' on the source slide.

muscles.name: Vastus Lateralis
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via the patellar tendon
muscles.actionText: Knee extension; helps stabilise the patella. Largest of the quadriceps.

muscles.name: Vastus Medialis
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via the patellar tendon
muscles.actionText: Knee extension; key to patellar tracking and knee stability.
muscles.clinical: Weakness contributes to poor patellar tracking and patellofemoral pain syndrome.

muscles.name: Vastus Intermedius
origin: Anterior and lateral surfaces of the femur
insertion: Tibial tuberosity via the patellar tendon
muscles.actionText: Knee extension, working in synergy with the other quadriceps.

muscles.name: Popliteus
origin: Lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle
insertion: Posterior surface of the tibia, above the soleal (popliteal) line
muscles.actionText: Unlocks the knee by laterally rotating the femur on the fixed tibia; assists knee flexion; stabilises the lateral meniscus.

muscles.name: Supraspinatus
muscles.actionText: Abducts the shoulder (first 15°) and stabilises the humeral head.

muscles.name: Infraspinatus
muscles.actionText: External rotation of the shoulder; stabilises the humeral head.

muscles.name: Teres Minor
muscles.actionText: External rotation of the shoulder; stabilises the humeral head.

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.actionText: Internal rotation of the shoulder; stabilises the humeral head.

muscles.name: Deltoid
muscles.actionText: Anterior fibres: flexion & medial rotation; middle: abduction; posterior: extension & lateral rotation.

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.actionText: Upper: elevates scapula; middle: retracts scapula; lower: depresses scapula; upper & lower together rotate the glenoid superiorly.

muscles.name: Levator Scapulae
insertion: Superior angle & medial border of scapula
muscles.actionText: Elevates the scapula and tilts the glenoid inferiorly.

muscles.name: Rhomboid Minor
insertion: Medial border of scapula (at level of the spine)
muscles.actionText: Retracts the scapula and rotates the glenoid inferiorly.

muscles.name: Rhomboid Major
insertion: Medial border of scapula, below the spine
muscles.actionText: Retracts the scapula and rotates the glenoid inferiorly.
muscles.notes: Named in the scapular movement tables but has no dedicated slide — origin/insertion filled from standard anatomy; verified against standard reference (CR-013): T2-T5 spinous process origin, medial scapular border insertion below the spine, dorsal scapular nerve C5, retraction/downward rotation actions all confirmed correct.

muscles.name: Serratus Anterior
insertion: Anterior surface of medial border of scapula
muscles.actionText: Protracts the scapula, rotates the glenoid superiorly and stabilises the scapula against the thorax.

muscles.name: Pectoralis Major
muscles.actionText: Adduction and medial rotation; clavicular head flexes; sternocostal head extends from a flexed position.

muscles.name: Pectoralis Minor
muscles.actionText: Stabilises the scapula; protraction and downward rotation. Assists rib elevation when the scapula is fixed.

muscles.name: Biceps Brachii
origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle & adjacent glenoid labrum
muscles.actionText: Elbow flexion, forearm supination and weak shoulder flexion.

muscles.name: Brachialis
muscles.actionText: Primary elbow flexor.

muscles.name: Coracobrachialis
muscles.actionText: Shoulder flexion and adduction; resists downward dislocation of the humerus.

muscles.name: Triceps Brachii
muscles.actionText: Elbow extension; the long head assists shoulder extension and adduction.

muscles.name: Anconeus
muscles.actionText: Assists elbow extension and stabilises the elbow joint.

muscles.name: Teres Major
insertion: Medial lip of intertubercular sulcus of humerus
muscles.actionText: Shoulder adduction, internal rotation and extension.

muscles.name: Latissimus Dorsi
insertion: Floor of intertubercular sulcus of humerus
muscles.actionText: Shoulder extension, adduction and internal rotation.

muscles.name: Diaphragm
muscles.actionText: Primary muscle of inspiration; flattens to expand the thoracic cavity.

muscles.name: External Intercostals
muscles.actionText: Elevate the ribs during inspiration; increase thoracic volume.

muscles.name: Internal Intercostals
muscles.actionText: Depress the ribs during forced expiration.
muscles.notes: Slide table was truncated in extraction — verified against standard reference (CR-013): origin/insertion were reversed (had rib-below to rib-above) relative to the standard convention used consistently for external-intercostals in this dataset; corrected to inferior border of rib above -> superior border of rib below. Nerve roots and expiration action confirmed correct.

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.actionText: Unilateral: rotates head to the opposite side and tilts to the same side. Bilateral: flexes the neck. Elevates the sternum in forced breathing.

muscles.name: Scalene Anterior
muscles.actionText: Elevates the 1st rib; lateral flexion of the neck.

muscles.name: Scalene Middle
muscles.actionText: Elevates the 1st rib; lateral flexion of the neck.

muscles.name: Scalene Posterior
muscles.actionText: Elevates the 2nd rib; lateral flexion of the neck.

muscles.name: Splenius Capitis
muscles.actionText: Extends, rotates and laterally flexes the head.
muscles.notes: Spelled 'Splenius Capitus' on the source slide.

muscles.name: Splenius Cervicis
muscles.actionText: Extends, rotates and laterally flexes the neck.

muscles.name: Iliocostalis
muscles.actionText: Extends and laterally flexes the vertebral column. Most lateral of the erector spinae.

muscles.name: Longissimus
muscles.actionText: Extends and laterally flexes the vertebral column and head. Longest of the erector spinae.

muscles.name: Spinalis
origin: Spinous processes of upper lumbar & lower thoracic vertebrae
insertion: Spinous processes of upper thoracic & cervical vertebrae
muscles.actionText: Extends the vertebral column. Smallest and most medial of the erector spinae.

muscles.name: Semispinalis
muscles.actionText: Extends the vertebral column and head; rotates contralaterally.

muscles.name: Multifidus
muscles.actionText: Stabilises the vertebrae; extends and rotates the spine.

muscles.name: Rotatores
origin: Transverse processes of the thoracic vertebrae
insertion: Base of spinous processes 1–2 segments above
muscles.actionText: Stabilises and rotates the vertebrae.

muscles.name: Interspinales
origin: Spinous processes of the cervical and lumbar vertebrae
muscles.actionText: Extends the vertebral column.

muscles.name: Intertransversarii
origin: Transverse processes of the cervical and lumbar vertebrae
muscles.actionText: Lateral flexion of the vertebral column.

muscles.name: Longus Colli
origin: Anterior bodies and transverse processes C3–T3
muscles.actionText: Flexes and slightly rotates the neck.

muscles.name: Longus Capitis
muscles.actionText: Flexes the head and neck.
muscles.notes: Spelled 'Longus Capitus' on the source slide.

muscles.name: Rectus Abdominis
muscles.actionText: Flexes the vertebral column and stabilises the pelvis.

muscles.name: External Oblique
muscles.actionText: Compresses the abdomen, rotates the trunk contralaterally, lateral flexion.

muscles.name: Internal Oblique
muscles.actionText: Compresses the abdomen, rotates the trunk ipsilaterally, lateral flexion.

muscles.name: Transversus Abdominis
muscles.actionText: Compresses the abdomen and stabilises the trunk.
muscles.notes: Written 'Transverse abdominis' on the source slide.

muscles.name: Quadratus Lumborum
muscles.actionText: Lateral flexion of the trunk; stabilises the 12th rib.
muscles.notes: The 'hip-hiker'; deep to erector spinae, between the 12th rib and pelvis.

muscles.name: Tibialis Anterior
origin: Lateral condyle and upper 2/3 of lateral tibia
muscles.actionText: Dorsiflexion and inversion of the foot; controls foot drop during walking.
muscles.clinical: Implicated in medial tibial stress syndrome and anterior compartment syndrome.

muscles.name: Extensor Hallucis Longus
insertion: Base of distal phalanx of big toe
muscles.actionText: Extends the big toe and dorsiflexes the foot.

muscles.name: Extensor Digitorum Longus
muscles.actionText: Extends toes 2–5 and dorsiflexes the foot.

muscles.name: Peroneus Tertius
muscles.actionText: Dorsiflexion and eversion of the foot.

muscles.name: Peroneus Longus
muscles.actionText: Eversion and plantarflexion; supports the arches of the foot.
muscles.clinical: Peroneal strengthening helps prevent inversion ankle sprains; site of peroneal tendinopathy.

muscles.name: Peroneus Brevis
muscles.actionText: Eversion and weak plantarflexion.
muscles.clinical: Peroneal tendinopathy behind the lateral malleolus; pain on resisted eversion.

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.actionText: Plantarflexion (especially with the knee extended) and knee flexion.
muscles.clinical: Achilles tendinopathy and rupture; tightness contributes to plantar fasciitis.

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.actionText: Plantarflexion, independent of knee position.
muscles.clinical: Involved in medial tibial stress syndrome and Achilles tendinopathy.

muscles.name: Plantaris
muscles.actionText: Weak plantarflexion and knee flexion.

muscles.name: Tibialis Posterior
muscles.actionText: Inversion and plantarflexion; supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.clinical: Key muscle in medial tibial stress syndrome.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Longus
muscles.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5 and assists plantarflexion.

muscles.name: Flexor Hallucis Longus
muscles.actionText: Flexes the big toe and assists plantarflexion.

muscles.name: Extensor Digitorum Brevis
origin: Dorsal and lateral surface of calcaneus
muscles.actionText: Extends digits 2–4.

muscles.name: Extensor Hallucis Brevis
muscles.actionText: Extends digit 1.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Brevis
muscles.actionText: Flexes toes 2–5 at the proximal interphalangeal joints.

muscles.name: Abductor Hallucis
insertion: Medial side of base of proximal phalanx of big toe
muscles.actionText: Abducts and flexes the big toe; supports the medial arch.

muscles.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi (Foot)
origin: Medial and lateral tubercles of calcaneus
insertion: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of 5th toe
muscles.actionText: Abducts and flexes the 5th toe.

muscles.name: Quadratus Plantae
origin: Medial and lateral sides of calcaneus
insertion: Posterolateral margin of tendon of flexor digitorum longus
muscles.actionText: Assists flexor digitorum longus in flexing toes 2–5.

muscles.name: Lumbricals (Foot)
insertion: Medial side of extensor expansions of toes 2–5
muscles.actionText: Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

muscles.name: Flexor Hallucis Brevis
origin: Plantar surfaces of cuboid and lateral cuneiform
insertion: Medial and lateral sides of the base of the proximal phalanx of the big toe
muscles.actionText: Flexes the big toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.notes: The two sesamoid bones of the foot sit within its tendons.

muscles.name: Adductor Hallucis
origin: Transverse head: plantar ligaments of MTP joints 3–5
insertion: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of big toe
muscles.actionText: Adducts the big toe; maintains the transverse arch.

muscles.name: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis (Foot)
insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of 5th toe
muscles.actionText: Flexes the 5th toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

muscles.name: Opponens Digiti Minimi (Foot)
muscles.actionText: Flexes the 5th toe; draws the metatarsal medially and downward.

muscles.name: Dorsal Interossei (Foot)
insertion: Proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of toes 2–4
muscles.actionText: Abduct toes 2–4 from the second toe axis; flex MTP joints and extend IP joints.

muscles.name: Plantar Interossei
muscles.actionText: Adduct toes 3–5 toward the second toe; flex MTP joints and extend IP joints.

muscles.name: Pronator Teres
muscles.actionText: Pronation of the forearm and weak elbow flexion.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis
muscles.actionText: Wrist flexion and radial deviation.
muscles.clinical: Common flexor origin at the medial epicondyle — golfer's elbow.

muscles.name: Palmaris Longus
muscles.actionText: Tenses the palmar fascia and assists wrist flexion.

muscles.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris
muscles.actionText: Wrist flexion and ulnar deviation.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis
muscles.actionText: Flexes the PIP joints of digits 2–5 and assists wrist flexion.

muscles.name: Flexor Digitorum Profundus
origin: Anterior and medial surfaces of ulna
muscles.actionText: Flexes the DIP joints of digits 2–5 and assists wrist flexion.

muscles.name: Flexor Pollicis Longus
muscles.actionText: Flexes the thumb at the IP joint.

muscles.name: Pronator Quadratus
muscles.actionText: Pronation of the forearm.

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.actionText: Flexes the forearm in a semi-pronated position (the handshake grip).

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus
muscles.actionText: Wrist extension and radial deviation.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis
muscles.actionText: Wrist extension and radial deviation.
muscles.clinical: Common extensor origin at the lateral epicondyle — tennis elbow.

muscles.name: Extensor Digitorum
muscles.actionText: Extends the MCP and IP joints of digits 2–5.

muscles.name: Extensor Digiti Minimi
muscles.actionText: Extends the MCP and IP joints of digit 5.

muscles.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris
muscles.actionText: Wrist extension and ulnar deviation.

muscles.name: Supinator
muscles.actionText: Supination of the forearm.

muscles.name: Abductor Pollicis Longus
origin: Posterior surfaces of ulna and radius
muscles.actionText: Abducts and extends the thumb at the CMC joint.

muscles.name: Extensor Pollicis Brevis
insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of thumb
muscles.actionText: Extends the thumb at the MCP joint.

muscles.name: Extensor Pollicis Longus
insertion: Base of distal phalanx of thumb
muscles.actionText: Extends the thumb at the IP joint.

muscles.name: Extensor Indicis
muscles.actionText: Extends the MCP and IP joints of digit 2.

muscles.name: Abductor Pollicis Brevis
insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of thumb
muscles.actionText: Abducts the thumb at the MCP joint.

muscles.name: Flexor Pollicis Brevis
insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of thumb
muscles.actionText: Flexes the thumb at the MCP joint.

muscles.name: Opponens Pollicis
muscles.actionText: Opposes the thumb.

muscles.name: Adductor Pollicis
insertion: Base of proximal phalanx of thumb
muscles.actionText: Adducts the thumb.

muscles.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi (Hand)
muscles.actionText: Abducts digit 5.

muscles.name: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis (Hand)
muscles.actionText: Flexes digit 5 at the MCP joint.

muscles.name: Opponens Digiti Minimi (Hand)
muscles.actionText: Opposes digit 5.

muscles.name: Lumbricals (Hand)
muscles.actionText: Flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints.

muscles.name: Dorsal Interossei (Hand)
muscles.actionText: Abduct the digits — DAB: Dorsal ABduct.

muscles.name: Palmar Interossei
muscles.actionText: Adduct the digits — PAD: Palmar ADduct.
